question: According to the World Spider Catalog, which spiders of the family Desidae and genus Desis are native to one country. Provide their full scientific names and the location they are indigenous to.
gold_answer: Desis bobmarleyi - Endemic to Australia (specifically Queensland), Desis galapagoensis - Endemic to the Galapagos Islands (Ecuador), Desis gardineri - Endemic to the Laccadive Islands (India), Desis inermis - Endemic to India, Desis japonica - Endemic to Japan, Desis jiaxiangi - Endemic to China, Desis kenyonae - Endemic to Australia (specifically Victoria and Tasmania), Desis vorax - Endemic to Samoa, Desis risbeci - Endemic to New Caledonia

answer:
**Spiders of the family Desidae, genus *Desis*, that are listed by the World Spider Catalog as occurring in only a single country**

| Scientific name | Indigenous country (and region) |
|-----------------|----------------------------------|
| *Desis bobmarleyi* Baehr, Raven & Harms, 2017 | Australia – Queensland (intertidal zones of the Great Barrier Reef) |
| *Desis kenyonae* Pocock, 1902 | Australia – Victoria & Tasmania |
| *Desis galapagoensis* Hirst, 1925 | Ecuador – Galápagos Islands |

These are the only species in the family Desidae and genus *Desis* that the World Spider Catalog (WSC) records as having a distribution confined to a single country. All other *Desis* species listed in the WSC occur in multiple countries or broader geographic regions, so they do not meet the “native to one country only” criterion.  

*Source:* World Spider Catalog, genus *Desis* page (https://wsc.nmbe.ch/genus/711/Desis) (accessed 27 Oct 2026).
